# Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation plays a positive role in the activation of Sonic Hedgehog pathway in mammals

- Hailong Wu<sup>1</sup>
- Steven Y Cheng<sup>2</sup>

## Abstract

Hedgehog signaling plays very important roles in development and cancers. Vertebrates have three transcriptional factors, Gli1, Gli2 and Gli3. Among them, Gli3 is a very special transcriptional factor which closely resembles Cubitus interruptus (Ci, in Drosophila) structurally and functionally as a ‘double agent’ for Shh target gene expression. Here we show that Gli3 full-length, but not the truncated form, can be methylated at K436 and K595. This methylation is specifically catalyzed by Set7, a lysine methyltransferase (KMT). Methylation at K436 and K595 respectively increases the stability and DNA binding ability of Gli3, resulting in an enhancement of Shh signaling activation. Furthermore, functional experiments indicate that the Gli3 methylation contributes to the tumor growth and metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer in vitro and in vivo. Therefore, we propose that Set7 mediated methylation is a novel PTM of Gli3, which positively regulates the transactivity of Gli3 and the activation of Shh signaling.

## Introduction

Hedgehog (Hh) signaling plays critical roles in embryonic development and tumor growth (Chen et al., 2007; Hooper and Scott, 2005; Ingham and McMahon, 2001; Nieuwenhuis and Hui, 2005; Yao and Chuang, 2015). Its misregulation leads to many types of cancers (Gialmanidis et al., 2009; Hui and Angers, 2011; Jiang and Hui, 2008). Hh pathway is activated when Hh ligands (Shh, Ihh or Dhh) bind to their repressive receptor Patched (Ptc), a twelve-transmembrane protein, leading to alleviation of its repression on the signaling transducer, Smoothened (Smo), a seven-transmembrane protein. The unleashed Smo can then activate the Gli transcription factors, resulting in the expression of downstream target genes, like Gli1 and Ptch1. In vertebrate, there are three Gli proteins, Gli1, Gli2 and Gli3. While Gli1 acts as a transcriptional activator and amplifies the Shh signal in a positive feedback loop, Gli2 and Gli3 mainly function as the Shh-regulated transcriptional activator and repressor. Among them, Gli3 draws considerable attentions due to its structural and functional similarity to Ci. Like Ci, Gli3 plays critical roles in modulating the switch-on and -off of Shh signaling. In the absence of Shh signaling, Gli3 is partially proteolyzed into a truncated transcriptional repressor (Gli3R) to block the expression of downstream target genes. In the presence of Shh signaling, Gli3 is in a full-length transactivation form and activates the expression of downstream genes like Gli1 and Ptch1 (Dai et al., 1999; 2002).

There is substantial evidence demonstrating that post-translational modifications (PTMs) play important roles in regulating protein functions, especially in regulating the transactivity of transcriptional factors (Filtz et al., 2014; Huang et al., 2013; Inuzuka et al., 2011; 2012; Liu et al., 2014; Munro et al., 2010). Like many other transcriptional factors, Gli3 is also subjected to various PTMs. Among them, phosphorylation and ubiquitination modifications are well characterized in regulating the transactivity of Gli3. For example, in the absence of Shh signal, Gli3 is phosphorylated by PKA, GSK3 and CKI, and subsequently ubiquitinated by SCFSlimb/β-TrcP for partial proteolyzation to confer it trans-repressive activity (Chen et al., 2009; Hsia et al., 2015; Tempé et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2000; Wang and Li, 2006; Zhang et al., 2009). Whether other PTMs are involved in the regulation of Gli3 transactivity remains elusive.

Protein methylation is one of the most common PTMs and plays an important role in regulating the transduction of signaling pathways, like MAPK, BMP, WNT, Hippo and JAK-STAT (Bikkavilli and Malbon, 2012; Kim et al., 2013; Mazur et al., 2014; Oudhoff et al., 2013; Viña et al., 2013). Protein methylation typically happens on arginine or lysine residues catalyzed by peptidylarginine methyltransferases (PRMTs) or lysine methyltransferases (KMTs) respectively. So far, near 50 KMTs and 9 PRMTs had been identified in human genome (Biggar and Li, 2015). Among them, Set7 is one of the most studied KMTs, regarding its pivotal role in methylation of non-histone proteins. Although Set7 was first identified as a histone lysine methyltransferase specifically for Histone 3 lysine 4 monomethylation, an epigenetic marker associated with transcriptional activation (Nishioka et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2001), accumulating evidence indicates that methylation of non-histone proteins including P53, P65, TAF10 and so on is the major biological function of this enzyme (Biggar and Li, 2015; Chuikov et al., 2004; Ea and Baltimore, 2009; Yang et al., 2009). Set7 mediated methylation of Lys372 in P53 increases its stability, resulting in the induction of P53 target genes (Chuikov et al., 2004). P65 can be methylated by Set7 at Lys37 which enhances the DNA binding and improves the expression of NF-κb target genes (Ea and Baltimore, 2009). Previous sequence alignments of the methylated sites on the initial substrates of Set7 revealed a predicted consensus sequence motif for Set7: (K/R)-(S/T/A)-K-X (Couture et al., 2006). Besides, a recent peptide-array based analysis redefined this recognition motif to: (G/R/H/K/P/S/T)-(K>R)-(S>K/Y/A/R/T/P/N)-K-(Q/N)-(A/Q/G/M/S/P/T/Y/V) (Dhayalan et al., 2011), which dramatically expands the putative targets of Set7.

Here, we report that Gli3 full-length, but not the Gli3 repression form, can be methylated at the K436 and K595 sites in vivo and in vitro. This methylation is specifically catalyzed by Set7. Moreover, the methylation modifications on K436 and K595 respectively increases the stability and the DNA binding capacity of Gli3, resulting in enhanced activation of Shh signaling pathway. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this Set7 mediated Gli3 methylations contribute to the tumor growth and metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer in vitro and in vivo. These findings expanded our understanding of PTM-directed Gli3 transactivity regulation, and implied a therapeutic potential of Set7 in treating tumors dependent on Shh signaling.

## Results

### Set7 methylates Gli3 full-length but not the repression form at K436 and K595 sites in vitro

Given that the transcriptional activity of Gli3 is orchestratedly regulated by multiple PTMs, such as phosphorylation and ubiquitination, and that protein methylation plays an important role in regulating several key signaling pathways, we sought to examine whether Gli3 can be post-translationally modified by methylation. We performed a mass spectrometry analysis of flag-tagged Gli3 from the cell lysate of HEK293T. This mass spectrometry analysis showed two methylation modifications on Gli3 K436 and K595 residues (Figure 1—figure supplement 1). By comparing the flanking sequence of K436 and K595 with reported Set7 substrates, such as ERα (Subramanian et al., 2008), P53 (Chuikov et al., 2004), PCAF (Masatsugu and Yamamoto, 2009) and Histone 3 (Wang et al., 2001), we found strong similarities among them (Figure 1A, upper panel), suggesting the possible involvement of Set7 in methylation of these two residues. Interestingly, these methylation signals were exclusively present in the Gli3 full-length but not the truncated repression form according to the mass spectrometry result (Figure 1—figure supplement 1). Through sequence alignments, we found that these two sites in Gli3 are evolutionally conserved in many species (Figure 1—figure supplement 2). To further test if the methylations on K436 and K595 are catalyzed by Set7, in vitro methylation assays were performed by incubating MBP-tagged peptides of Gli3, MBP-K436 (amino acids from 344 to 463 of Gli3) or MBP-K595 (amino acids from 464 to 666 of Gli3) with GST-Set7 and 3H-SAM (Figure 1A, lower panel). As shown in Figure 1B, Set7 can specifically methylate the peptides, MBP-K436 and MBP-K595, whereas the substitution of K436 or K595 with arginine (K436R or K595R) abolished Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation. In addition, GST pull-down assays further indicated the interaction between Set7 and Gli3 (Figure 1C).

### Set7 methylates Gli3 at K436 and K595 in vivo

To facilitate studies on the Set7-mediated methylation of Gli3 in vivo, we generated polyclonal antibodies that specifically recognize monomethylated Gli3-K436 or Gli3-K595, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A). Dot plot assays confirmed the specificity of those antibodies (Figure 1—figure supplement 3). Consistent with the results of mass spectrometry, immunoprecipitation (IP) of endogenous Gli3 in HEK293T cells followed by immunoblot showed that only the full-length Gli3 contains the methylation signals on Gli3-K436 and Gli3-K595 (Figure 1D). The methylation signals were decreased upon Set7 knockdown, indicating that methylation on these two sites of Gli3 is mediated by Set7 (Figure 1D). Moreover, overexpression of Set7 drastically improved the methylation levels whereas the catalytically inactive mutant of Set7, Set7H297A (Wang et al., 2001), had no effect on those methylations of Gli3 (Figure 1E). Furthermore, Set7 failed to methylate Gli3K436R or Gli3K595R, the arginine substitution mutants of Gli3, in vivo (Figure 1F).

Since the methylation happens exclusively in the full-length Gli3, which acts as a principal transcription activator of Shh pathway in response to Shh signal (Dai et al., 1999), we then adopted, NIH-3T3, a cell line fully responsive to the Shh signaling, to perform our further investigation. Cells with stable expression of individual unrelated Set7 shRNAs showed significantly reduced methylation signals on K436 and K595 of Gli3 compared to cells expressing luciferase control shRNA (Figure 1G). In addition, the Gli3 arginine substitution mutants, Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R, showed abolished methylation signals when blotted with the matched antibodies (Figure 1H). Given that only the full-length Gli3 can be methylated, we began to use a Gli3PA mutant, in which the six phosphorylatable serines in the PKA target clusters were mutated to nonphosphorylatable alanines, resulting in the resistance of Gli3PA to be processed into Gli3R (Niewiadomski et al., 2014) (Figure 1I'). Similar to the result in Figure 1H, the methylation signals can be detected in Gli3PA but not in its arginine substitution mutants, Gli3PAK436R and Gli3PAK595R when blotted with respective antibodies (Figure 1I). Given the Shh signaling plays an important role in the development of multiple embryonic tissues of mice (Ingham and McMahon, 2001), we started to examine whether these methylation signals exist in the Gli3 in several responsive mouse embryonic tissues, such as brain, lung, skin, skeleton and gut. Indicated tissues were collected from embryos 14.5 days post coitum (dpc) and Gli3 methylation signals were detected by western blot using anti-Gli3 antibody, Me-K436 antibody and Me-K595 antibody, respectively. As shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4, the methylation signals on Gli3 full length were only detected in embryonic lung tissues. Since Gli3 full-length can be methylated by Set7 in vivo and in vitro, we then examined whether Set7 interacts with Gli3. GST pull-down assays indicated that GST-tagged Set7 can successfully pull down the flag-tagged Gli3 full-length of NIH-3T3 cells in the presence of Shh (Figure 1J). Therefore, we demonstrate that Set7 can methylate the full-length, but not the repression form of Gli3, at K436 and K595 residues, indicating that Gli3 is a novel substrate of Set7.

### Set7 positively regulates the activation of Shh signaling by methylating Gli3

Set7 can modulate the activation of multiple signaling pathways, such as NF-κb, JAK-STAT, we sought to examine whether Set7 also regulates Shh signaling. We performed Shh luciferase reporter assays (Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1990) in the condition of Set7 knockdown. In the absence of Shh, downregulation of Set7 had no effect on the luciferase activity. In contrast, Set7 knockdown dramatically decreased the luciferase activity in the presence of Shh, suggesting that Set7 plays a positive role on Shh pathway activation but has no effect on the basal level of Shh signaling (Figure 2A and A’). In line with this finding, overexpression of Set7 but not its inactive mutant Set7H297A can significantly enhance the luciferase activity in the presence of Shh (Figure 2B), suggesting that its methyltransferase activity is required for Set7 mediated Shh activation. Furthermore, Set7 mediated increase of luciferase activity was in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2C). We then examined whether Set7 knockdown affects the expression of endogenous Shh target genes, like Gli1 and Ptch1. In the presence of Shh, NIH-3T3 cells expressing Set7 siRNAs showed significant reduction in Set7 protein levels and a parallel decrease in Gli1 and Ptch1 mRNA levels compared to cells expressing control siRNAs (Figure 2D–F). In addition, Gli1 protein level was also decrease in cells with Set7 knockdown (Figure 2F). It’s of interest that either Shh or SAG, the agonist of Shh pathway, directed activation of Shh signaling can upregulate Set7 levels, whereas Gli1 knockdown can lead to a decrease of Set7 mRNA levels, suggesting the existence of a potential positive feedback loop between Set7 and Shh signaling (Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 1). In addition, NIH-3T3 cells treated with Shh showed greatly increased methylation signals on Gli3 which may be probably due to increased Gli3 full-length or/and Set7 levels (Figure 2A’ and Figure 2—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the methylation signals of Gli3 is regulated by Shh input. Taken together, these findings indicate that Set7 can positively regulate the activation of Shh signaling.

Next, we started to investigate whether the positive regulation of Set7 on Shh signaling relies on its methylation on Gli3. As shown in Figure 2G, although Set7 knockdown can suppress the activation of Shh signaling, this inhibition was abolished when the Gli3 level was depleted by RNAi. In contrast, depletion of both Gli1 and Gli2 in MEF cells showed no effect on releasing such inhibition due to Set7 knockdown (Figure 2—figure supplement 3). These findings apparently indicate the requirement of Gli3 on Set7 mediated Shh activation. Furthermore, compared to Gli3WT, the mRNA levels of Gli1 and Ptch1 and the Shh luciferase activity were decreased in cells expressing Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R, suggesting that Set7-directed Gli3 methylation plays an important role in maintaining Shh activation (Figure 2H–J). In consistent with this finding, cells expressing the Gli3PA point mutants, Gli3PAK436R and Gli3PAK595R, showed decreased Shh luciferase activity and levels of Gli1 and Ptch1 transcripts compared to those with Gli3PAWT expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 4). To further confirm this notion, Shh luciferase reporter assays were performed. Either Set7 downregulation or upregulation can lead to the reduction or the induction of Shh luciferase activity respectively in cells with Gli3WT expression but not in cells expressing Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R (Figure 2K and L). Thus, our findings strongly suggested that Gli3 methylation at K436 and K595 sites are required for Set7-mediated enhancement of Shh signaling activation.

### Methylation by Set7 improves the stability and DNA binding ability of Gli3 full-length

Gli3 can be regulated at multiple levels to affect the transduction of Shh signaling, such as trafficking to the primary cilium, changes of protein stability or binding ability to the promoters of target genes. In mammal, the primary cilium (cilia) is an essential organelle for Shh signaling transduction. Gli3 traffics in and out of the cilia all the time (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B). In the presence of Shh, Gli3 initially accumulates in the cilium tip (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and then functions as Gli3A to bind to the promoter of Gli1 to further transduce the signaling (Chen et al., 2009; Dai et al., 1999; 2002; Wen et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2009). In order to verify whether Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation affects its cilial translocation, we performed cilial staining in Shh treated NIH-3T3 cells with stable expression of Set7 shRNA, Set7 or Set7H297A. As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D, the Gli3 accumulation on the tips of cilia was comparable among those three groups, suggesting that the Set7-related changes of Shh activation are not due to the cilial translocation of Gli3.

It has been reported that Set7 can influence the stability of its methylated substrates like P53 (Chuikov et al., 2004). Given the importance of Gli3 stability on Shh signaling activation (Tempé et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2009), we then tested whether Set7 can also affect the stability of Gli3. Western blot showed that knockdown of Set7 caused a significant reduction of endogenous Gli3 at protein levels (Figure 3A, left panel), whereas overexpression of Set7 improved the Gli3 protein level (Figure 3A, right panel). This Set7 mediated induction of Gli3 seems due to PTMs, because the mRNA level of Gli3 had no change regardless whether Set7 was knocked down or overexpressed (Figure 3B). To further confirm this point, we then tested whether Set7 can affect the protein levels of the unmethylatable Gli3 mutants, Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R. As expected, exogenous Gli3WT had the same change as the endogenous Gli3. Interestingly, like the Gli3WT, the protein levels of Gli3K595R were still subjected to the modulation of Set7, whereas the protein levels of Gli3K436R were not responding to either knockdown or overexpression of Set7 (Figure 3C and D). These findings suggested that the methylation at K436 but not K595 causes stability change of Gli3 (Figure 3C and D). Finally, the reduced half-life of Gli3K436R, but not Gli3WT or Gli3K595R was defined by western blot in cells treated with cycloheximide (CHX) (Figure 3E and F). Therefore, these data indicated that Set7 mediated methylation on K436 increases the protein stability of Gli3.

Gli3 full-length is a transcription activator and can bind to the promoter of Gli1 to further enhance the activation of Shh signaling (Hui and Angers, 2011; Jiang and Hui, 2008). To examine whether Set7 also affects the DNA binding ability of Gli3, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assays were performed in NIH-3T3 cells in the presence of Shh. As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2, knockdown of Set7 greatly decreased the binding of Gli3 on Gli1’s promoter regions (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2). Although Shh treatment can almost completely block the processing of Gli3 full-length to Gli3R, trace Gli3R background may still disturb the result of ChIP assays. In order to address this concern, we established NIH-3T3 cell lines with stable expression of C-terminal flag-tagged Gli3 (Gli3-flag). Thus, only the Gli3 full-length can be recognized by anti-flag antibody. ChIP assays with anti-flag antibody demonstrated that Set7 knockdown markedly affected the binding of Gli3 on Gli1’s promoter regions (Figure 3G–I), suggesting that Set7 augments the DNA binding of Gli3 full-length. Given that K595 is on the zinc finger which is important for DNA binding of Gli3 (Pavletich and Pabo, 1993), it’s conceivable that the Set7 mediated methylation on K595 may contribute to increased DNA binding of Gli3. Stable cell lines expressing Gli3WT-flag, Gli3 mutants (Gli3K436R-flag and Gli3K595R-flag) were established. Comparable expression of flag-tagged Gli3 was detected in those three cell lines (Figure 3J). ChIP assays with anti-flag antibody showed dramatically impaired the DNA binding ability in Gli3K595R-flag, whereas the Gli3K436R-flag presented the similar DNA binding ability to Gli3WT-flag (Figure 3K), suggesting that Set7 mediated methylation at K595 enhances the DNA binding ability of Gli3. In addition, the binding ability of Gli3 was also examined in the promoter regions of Ptch1 and Hhip by ChIP assays. As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3, the binding of Gli3 to these regions was markedly impaired after Set7 knockdown. In conclusion, Set7 improved the protein stability and DNA binding ability of Gli3 through methylation of K436 and K595 sites respectively.

### The methylation of Gli3 positively regulates tumorigenesis in NSCLCs

Misregulation of Shh pathway has been reported in many types of cancers, including basal cell carcinoma, medulloblastoma and lung cancer (Gialmanidis et al., 2009; Hui and Angers, 2011; Jiang and Hui, 2008; Yuan et al., 2007). Since Set7 can augment Shh activation by increasing Gli3 stability and its DNA binding ability on the promoter regions of Gli1, we then determined whether this Set7-Gli3-Gli1 axis plays a role in tumor development. By comparison on the mRNA levels of Set7 and Gli1 between Beas2B, a normal bronchial epithelial lung cell line, and A549, a non-small cell lung cancer cell line, we found that both Set7 and Gli1 were extensively expressed in A549 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A). Furthermore, the GEO database search (GSE10245) showed a positive association between Set7 and Gli1 in NSCLC tumor samples, suggesting the involvement of this Set7-Gli3-Gli1 axis in the development of NSCLCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B). To examine the existence of this regulation axis in A549 cells, we performed Shh luciferase reporter assays and qPCR to evaluate the activity of Shh signaling in A549 cells with Set7 knockdown. Depletion of Set7 displayed a decreased luciferase activity and reduced expression of Gli1 and Ptch1 (Figure 4A and B). Our above findings indicate that unmethylatable mutations at either K436 or K595 cause a significant reduction of Shh signaling activation (Figure 2H–J). To examine whether unmethylatable mutations at both sites will lead to a synergistic suppression on Shh signaling activation, we constructed a double arginine substitution mutant of Gli3, Gli3KRKR, in which both K436 and K595 were mutated to arginine. To further examine whether Gli3 methylations at K436 and K595 are important for Set7-mediated Shh activation in A549 cells, we performed luciferase assays and qPCR. Compared to A549 cells with stable Gli3WT expression, reduced luciferase activity and transcripts of Gli1 and Ptch1 were detected in cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR (Figure 4C–E). In addition, more severe suppression on luciferase activities and Ptch1 mRNA, but not Gli1 mRNA, was observed in cells expressing Gli3KRKR, suggesting that the methylation at these two sites plays a synergistic role in regulating Shh signaling activation (Figure 4D and E). In line with the reduced Shh activation, MTT assays showed attenuated growth in cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR compared to cells with Gli3WT expression (Figure 4F). Since anchorage-independent growth is tightly associated with tumor development, we then determined whether Set7-mediated Gli3 methylation affects this feature. The ability to form colonies in soft agar was dramatically impaired in stable transfectants with the expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR compared to Gli3WT (Figure 4G and G’). In agreement with these in vitro growth assays, A549 cells with stable expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR showed retarded tumor growth in a xenograft tumor model (Figure 4H–J).

## Discussion

In present study, we demonstrated that Set7 can exclusively methylate Gli3 full-length at K436 and K595 sites in vitro and in vivo. These methylations on Gli3 augment the activation of Shh signaling. To our knowledge, we for the first time identified Gli3 as a novel substrate of Set7 and demonstrated the involvement of Set7 in Shh activation. Furthermore, we showed that Set7 mediated methylation on K436 increases the protein stability of Gli3 whereas the methylation on K595 boosts the DNA binding of Gli3. Finally, functional experiments indicated that this Set7-mediated Gli3 methylation contributes to the tumor growth and metastasis in NSCLCs in vitro and in vivo.

Hh signaling is one of the most conserved signaling pathways. The silence or activation of Hh signaling is tightly regulated by various post-translational modifications (PTMs) at multiple levels. Gli3 is a key transcriptional factor determining the switch-off and -on of Shh signaling. The PTMs of Gli3 like phosphorylation (Tempé et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2000; Wang and Li, 2006) and ubiquitination (Chen et al., 2009; Hsia et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2009) are largely involved in this process. For example, in the absence of Shh, Gli3 full-length is phosphorylated by PKA, GSK3 and CK1 and is subjected to SCFSlimb/β-TrcP mediated ubiquitination followed with partial proteasome degradation to generate a truncated repression form, Gli3R (Tempé et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2000; Wang and Li, 2006).

Protein methylation, as one of the most common PTMs, participates in the regulation of signaling transduction of multiple signaling pathways, like MAPK, BMP, WNT, Hippo and JAK-STAT (Bikkavilli and Malbon, 2012; Kim et al., 2013; Mazur et al., 2014; Oudhoff et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2013). Protein methylation is catalyzed by methyltransferase. Among them, Set7 draws tremendous attention to its predominant role in methylating non-histone proteins. In this study, we identify that Gli3 is a novel substrate of Set7. By methylating Gli3, Set7 positively regulates the activation of Shh signaling pathway.

It’s of particular interest that, although Gli3R also has these two residues, K436 and K595, the Set7 mediated methylation solely occurs in Gli3 full-length. One possible explanation comes from the differential cellular localization of Gli3R and Gli3 full-length in the absence of Shh. A recent study demonstrates that the stability of Dnmt1 can be dynamically regulated by Set7 and demethylase, Lsd1 (Wang et al., 2009). Since Lsd1 is a nuclear protein, it is conceivable that Lsd1 can also remove the methylation modifications of Gli3R, resulting in these signals undetectable either by mass spectrometry or western blot. In addition, we found increased Set7 levels in cells treated with Shh or SAG, suggesting a positive feedback loop between Set7 and Shh signaling. Thus, in the presence of Shh signaling, although Gli3 full-length also translocates into the nucleus subjected to Lsd1 mediated demethylation, increased Set7 could possibly compensate this demethylation effect, resulting in augment in Shh signaling. Therefore, it will be particularly interesting to examine whether Lsd1 and Set7 can dynamically regulate the activation of Shh signaling by demethylation and methylation of Gli3 respectively.

We demonstrated that Set7 methylates K436 and K595 of Gli3. The methylation on K436 increases the protein stability and the methylation on K595 enhances the DNA binding of Glli3. These two methylation modifications of Gli3 are not redundant, because arginine substitution in either point severely impairs the activation of Shh signaling, suggesting the role of Set7 in fine-tuning the transactivity of Gli3.

It has been recently reported that the activation of Shh signaling represses the canonical WNT signaling in colon epithelial cell differentiation, and that WNT pathway activation negatively regulates Shh pathway (van den Brink et al., 2004; Yanai et al., 2008), suggesting a mutual repelling crosstalk between these two pathways. Given that Set7 can inhibit WNT signaling by methylating β-catenin, and activate Shh signaling by methylating Gli3, it’s very possible that Set7 is a key regulator involved in this WNT-Shh crosstalk.

Abnormal activation of Shh signaling contributes to tumor development by promoting cell proliferation and EMT in many cancer types. Our present study indicates that Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation is critical for this oncogenic role of Shh pathway because cancer cells expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR showed severely reduced growth and metastasis in xenograft tumor models. This finding strongly suggests a therapeutic value of Ser7 in targeting Shh-dependent tumors, such as BCC, MB and Lung cancer.

HEK293T, A549 and NIH-3T3 were purchased from Cell Bank, The Culture Collection, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CBTCCCAS). CBTCCCAS has provided certifications for the source, identity and mycoplasma contamination of these cell lines. HEK293T cells and A549 cells were cultured in DMEM medium (HyClone, Logan, UT) with 10% FBS (Gibco, Wellesley Hills, MA) and transfected with Lipofectamine2000 (Invitrogen, Waltham, MA) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. ### Immunoprecipitation and western blot

HEK293T cells were lysed using NP-40 buffer (50 mM Tris-Cl pH8.0, 0.1 M NaCl, 10 mM Sodium fluoride, 1 mM Sodium vanadate, 1% NP-40, 10% Glycerol, 1.5 mM EDTA, Protease Inhibitor Cocktail). Cell lysates were rotated for 30 min at 4°C and cleared by centrifuge at full speed. Lysates were then incubated with M2 beads (Sigma-Aldrich, St Louis, MO) for 24 hr at 4°C. After 4-time wash (15 min/time) with NP-40 buffer, the protein samples were collected by boiling in 1×SDS loading buffer and subjected to standard SDS-PAGE and Western Blot. Primary antibodies used in this study: Mouse anti-flag (Sigma-Aldrich), Mouse anti-Set7 (Cell signaling, Danvers, MA), Goat anti-Gli3 (R&D), Rabbit anti-GAPDH (Sigma-Aldrich), Rabbit anti-monomethylated K436 (Me-K436, Abcolony, China), Rabbit anti-monomethylated K595 (Me-K595, Abcolony, China). ### Mass spectrometry

Flag tagged Gli3 were transfected into the HEK293T cells. Cells were collected 48 hr after transfection. Then IP flag using M2 beads as described above. The protein samples were digested by Filter Aided Sample Preparation (FASP) Method (Wisniewski et al., 2009). The tryptic peptides were separated by nanoflow liquid chromatography and analyzed by tandem mass spectrometry (Thermo Electron Finnigan). The LTQ-Orbitrap equipped with an NSI nanospray source (1.5 kV) was operated in data-dependent mode, in which the normalized collision energy was 35%. Full scan was detected in the Orbitrap analyzer (R=60,000 at m/z 300) followed by MS/MS acquisition of the ten most-intense ions in LTQ. Mass calibration used an internal lock mass (m/z 445.120025), the dynamic exclusion repeat count was 1, the repeat duration was 30 s, and the exclusion duration window was 120 s. Raw Orbitrap full-scan MS and ion trap MS2 spectra were processed by MaxQuant 1.3.0.5 (Cox and Mann, 2008). A composite target-decoy database was created with the program Sequence Reverser from the MaxQuant package. All identified MS/MS spectra were searched against this target/decoy database (Human UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot database, 2014-10-29 download). Spectra were initially searched with a mass tolerance of 7 ppm in MS and 0.5 Da in MS/MS and strict trypsin specificity. Cysteine carbamidomethylation was searched as a fixed modification, whereas N-acetyl protein, oxidized methionine, and mono-methylated lysine (putative methylation site) were searched as variable modification. The estimated false discovery rate (FDR) of all peptide and protein identifications was fixed at maximum 1% (Olsen et al., 2006).

### Wound healing assay

Cells (5×105) were seeded in 3.5 cm dishes and incubated overnight. The cell monolayers were scratched horizontally using a sterile 10 μl pipette tip. ### Soft agar assay

Briefly, 1ml culture medium with 1% agar was first plated into 3.5 cm dishes. After the bottom agar became solidified, each well received another 1 ml 0.3% agar in culture medium carrying 5000 cells. Cells were covered with 1 ml of complete medium and medium was changed every four days. Colonies were stained with 0.005% crystal violet and counted after 3-weeks of incubation.

### Transwell migration assay

The transwell migration assay was carried out using a 24-well transwell cell culture chamber (Corning, New York) with an 8 μm pore size. Briefly, 1×104 cells were added into an upper chamber with 200 μl DMEM without serum. 700 μl DMEM containing 20% FBS was added into the lower chamber as a chemo attractant. After 48 hr, the non-migration cells were manually removed with a rubber swab. Cells that migrated to the lower side of the membrane were stained with crystal violet and photographed using an inverted microscope.

### Transwell invasion assay

The transwell invasion assay was carried out using a 24-well transwell cell culture chamber (Corning, New York). The 8 μm pore size upper chambers were coated with growth factor-reduced Matrigel (BD). Briefly, A549 cells were incubate in serum free medium for 24 hr. Matrigel were diluted three times with serum free DMEM. Add 50 μl above mixture to the upper chamber and incubate for at least 4 hr. Then 2×104 cells were added into an upper chamber with 200 μl DMEM without serum. 700 μl DMEM containing 20% FBS was added into the lower chamber as a chemoattractant. After 48 hr, the non-invasion cells were manually removed with a rubber swab. Cells that invade to the lower side of the membrane were stained with crystal violet and photographed using an inverted microscope.

### Tumor formation assay

Exponential phase A549 cells were trypsinized and washed with PBS (HyClone) and suspended in fresh PBS in 4°C. 5X106 cells were injected subcutaneously into four-week-old female nude mice on both left and right flank. Tumor size was measured every 7 days, and tumor volume was estimated using the formula: tumor volume=0.5×length×width2. At the end of this experiment, tumors were harvested, weighed and photographed. Summary:

Fu et al. investigate the potential methylation regulation of Hh-Gli signaling. They show that Gli3 can be methylated at K436 and K595 by the lysine methyltransferase Set7, leading to enhanced stability and DNA binding activity. The results linking posttranslational methylation to Gli function are interesting and have potential cancer relevance. However, the authors need to address several issues to confirm their conclusions and demonstrate their physiological relevance.

Essential revisions:

1) All of the RNAi experiments need to be done with at least two unrelated siRNAs or shRNAs. This is done in some but not all experiments. For example, the use of two siRNAs or shRNAs appears to be missing in Figures: 1G, 2G, K and 3A, B, H.

2) The authors claim that Set7 methylates full-length Gli3, but not the truncated repressor form. However, this is hard to assess in several of the current immunoblots. High-quality immunoblots of Figure 1E, F, G and H should be provided. In addition, the authors should also test whether Set7 can methylate the Gli3 truncated form when ectopically expressed.

3) With the available K436/K595 antibodies, the authors should examine whether methylation at these sites occurs in vivo in responsive tissues in mice or fly. Please let us know if you have access to these tissue samples and the time frame for you to complete an experimental test of Gli3 methylation in vivo.

4) Figure 3. ChIP-qPCR should be carried out on other well-established Gli targets in addition to the sites in the Gli1 promoter.

Desirable but not essential revisions:

1) Is the level of methylation regulated by Hedgehog ligand input?

2) The importance of the manuscript would be strengthened if the authors could demonstrate that the Set7-Gli3 regulation occurs in canonical Hh tumors, such as BCC and MB.

3) Gli3 has been reported to function both as a transcriptional activator and a repressor. Therefore, the strong pro-oncogenic effect of Gli3 in the presented xenografts experiments may be a bit surprising. Can the authors comment on this issue?

claims.evidence: Shown by cycloheximide chase experiments and western blot analysis in Figure 3.

claims.claim: Methylation at K595 increases the DNA binding ability of Gli3.
claims.source: Methylation at K436 and K595 respectively increases the stability and DNA binding ability of Gli3, resulting in an enhancement of Shh signaling activation.
claims.evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP assays showing reduced DNA binding in Gli3K595R mutant.

claims.claim: Gli3 methylation contributes to tumor growth and metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer in vitro and in vivo.
claims.source: Furthermore, functional experiments indicate that the Gli3 methylation contributes to the tumor growth and metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer in vitro and in vivo.
claims.evidence: Supported by MTT assays, soft agar assays, xenograft tumor models, and migration/invasion assays in Figure 4.

claims.claim: Set7 mediated methylation is a novel PTM of Gli3 that positively regulates the transactivity of Gli3 and the activation of Shh signaling.
claims.source: Therefore, we propose that Set7 mediated methylation is a novel PTM of Gli3, which positively regulates the transactivity of Gli3 and the activation of Shh signaling.
claims.evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assays and qPCR showing increased Shh target gene expression.

claims.claim: Hedgehog signaling plays critical roles in embryonic development and tumor growth.
claims.source: Hedgehog (Hh) signaling plays critical roles in embryonic development and tumor growth (Chen et al., 2007; Hooper and Scott, 2005; Ingham and McMahon, 2001; Nieuwenhuis and Hui, 2005; Yao and Chuang, 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.

claims.claim: Misregulation of Hedgehog signaling leads to many types of cancers.
claims.source: Its misregulation leads to many types of cancers (Gialmanidis et al., 2009; Hui and Angers, 2011; Jiang and Hui, 2008).
claims.evidence: Supported by literature citations.

claims.claim: Gli3 plays critical roles in modulating the switch-on and -off of Shh signaling.
claims.source: Like Ci, Gli3 plays critical roles in modulating the switch-on and -off of Shh signaling.
claims.evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about Gli3 function.

claims.claim: In the absence of Shh signaling, Gli3 is partially proteolyzed into a truncated transcriptional repressor (Gli3R).
claims.source: In the absence of Shh signaling, Gli3 is partially proteolyzed into a truncated transcriptional repressor (Gli3R) to block the expression of downstream target genes.
claims.evidence: Supported by literature citations (Dai et al., 1999; 2002).

claims.claim: In the presence of Shh signaling, Gli3 is in a full-length transactivation form and activates the expression of downstream genes like Gli1 and Ptch1.
claims.source: In the presence of Shh signaling, Gli3 is in a full-length transactivation form and activates the expression of downstream genes like Gli1 and Ptch1 (Dai et al., 1999; 2002).
claims.evidence: Supported by literature citations.

claims.claim: Post-translational modifications play important roles in regulating protein functions, especially in regulating the transactivity of transcriptional factors.
claims.source: There is substantial evidence demonstrating that post-translational modifications (PTMs) play important roles in regulating protein functions, especially in regulating the transactivity of transcriptional factors (Filtz et al., 2014; Huang et al., 2013; Inuzuka et al., 2011; 2012; Liu et al., 2014; Munro et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.

claims.claim: In the absence of Shh signal, Gli3 is phosphorylated by PKA, GSK3 and CKI, and subsequently ubiquitinated by SCFSlimb/β-TrcP for partial proteolyzation.
claims.source: For example, in the absence of Shh signal, Gli3 is phosphorylated by PKA, GSK3 and CKI, and subsequently ubiquitinated by SCFSlimb/β-TrcP for partial proteolyzation to confer it trans-repressive activity (Chen et al., 2009; Hsia et al., 2015; Tempé et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2000; Wang and Li, 2006; Zhang et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.

claims.claim: Protein methylation plays an important role in regulating the transduction of signaling pathways, like MAPK, BMP, WNT, Hippo and JAK-STAT.
claims.source: Protein methylation is one of the most common PTMs and plays an important role in regulating the transduction of signaling pathways, like MAPK, BMP, WNT, Hippo and JAK-STAT (Bikkavilli and Malbon, 2012; Kim et al., 2013; Mazur et al., 2014; Oudhoff et al., 2013; Viña et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.

claims.claim: Near 50 KMTs and 9 PRMTs had been identified in human genome.
claims.source: So far, near 50 KMTs and 9 PRMTs had been identified in human genome (Biggar and Li, 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: Set7 was first identified as a histone lysine methyltransferase specifically for Histone 3 lysine 4 monomethylation.
claims.source: Although Set7 was first identified as a histone lysine methyltransferase specifically for Histone 3 lysine 4 monomethylation, an epigenetic marker associated with transcriptional activation (Nishioka et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2001), accumulating evidence indicates that methylation of non-histone proteins including P53, P65, TAF10 and so on is the major biological function of this enzyme (Biggar and Li, 2015; Chuikov et al., 2004; Ea and Baltimore, 2009; Yang et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by literature citations (Nishioka et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2001).

claims.claim: Set7 mediated methylation of Lys372 in P53 increases its stability, resulting in the induction of P53 target genes.
claims.source: Set7 mediated methylation of Lys372 in P53 increases its stability, resulting in the induction of P53 target genes (Chuikov et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: P65 can be methylated by Set7 at Lys37 which enhances the DNA binding and improves the expression of NF-κb target genes.
claims.source: P65 can be methylated by Set7 at Lys37 which enhances the DNA binding and improves the expression of NF-κb target genes (Ea and Baltimore, 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by literature citation.

claims.claim: Mass spectrometry analysis showed two methylation modifications on Gli3 K436 and K595 residues.
claims.source: This mass spectrometry analysis showed two methylation modifications on Gli3 K436 and K595 residues (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Directly observed in mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The flanking sequences of K436 and K595 show strong similarities with reported Set7 substrates.
claims.source: By comparing the flanking sequence of K436 and K595 with reported Set7 substrates, such as ERα (Subramanian et al., 2008), P53 (Chuikov et al., 2004), PCAF (Masatsugu and Yamamoto, 2009) and Histone 3 (Wang et al., 2001), we found strong similarities among them (Figure 1A, upper panel), suggesting the possible involvement of Set7 in methylation of these two residues.
claims.evidence: Shown by sequence alignment in Figure 1A and supported by literature citations.

claims.claim: Methylation signals were exclusively present in the Gli3 full-length but not the truncated repression form according to the mass spectrometry result.
claims.source: Interestingly, these methylation signals were exclusively present in the Gli3 full-length but not the truncated repression form according to the mass spectrometry result (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Observed in mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: K436 and K595 sites in Gli3 are evolutionally conserved in many species.
claims.source: Through sequence alignments, we found that these two sites in Gli3 are evolutionally conserved in many species (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Shown by sequence alignment in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Set7 can specifically methylate the peptides, MBP-K436 and MBP-K595.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 1B, Set7 can specifically methylate the peptides, MBP-K436 and MBP-K595, whereas the substitution of K436 or K595 with arginine (K436R or K595R) abolished Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation.
claims.evidence: Demonstrated by in vitro methylation assay shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: Substitution of K436 or K595 with arginine (K436R or K595R) abolished Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 1B, Set7 can specifically methylate the peptides, MBP-K436 and MBP-K595, whereas the substitution of K436 or K595 with arginine (K436R or K595R) abolished Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation.
claims.evidence: Demonstrated by in vitro methylation assay shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: GST pull-down assays indicated the interaction between Set7 and Gli3.
claims.source: In addition, GST pull-down assays further indicated the interaction between Set7 and Gli3 (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: Shown by GST pull-down assay in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Only the full-length Gli3 contains the methylation signals on Gli3-K436 and Gli3-K595.
claims.source: Consistent with the results of mass spectrometry, immunoprecipitation (IP) of endogenous Gli3 in HEK293T cells followed by immunoblot showed that only the full-length Gli3 contains the methylation signals on Gli3-K436 and Gli3-K595 (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: The methylation signals on Gli3 were decreased upon Set7 knockdown.
claims.source: The methylation signals were decreased upon Set7 knockdown, indicating that methylation on these two sites of Gli3 is mediated by Set7 (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: Shown by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Set7 drastically improved the methylation levels whereas the catalytically inactive mutant of Set7, Set7H297A, had no effect on those methylations of Gli3.
claims.source: Moreover, overexpression of Set7 drastically improved the methylation levels whereas the catalytically inactive mutant of Set7, Set7H297A (Wang et al., 2001), had no effect on those methylations of Gli3 (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Set7 failed to methylate Gli3K436R or Gli3K595R, the arginine substitution mutants of Gli3, in vivo.
claims.source: Furthermore, Set7 failed to methylate Gli3K436R or Gli3K595R, the arginine substitution mutants of Gli3, in vivo (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: Shown by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: Cells with stable expression of Set7 shRNAs showed significantly reduced methylation signals on K436 and K595 of Gli3.
claims.source: Cells with stable expression of individual unrelated Set7 shRNAs showed significantly reduced methylation signals on K436 and K595 of Gli3 compared to cells expressing luciferase control shRNA (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: Gli3 arginine substitution mutants, Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R, showed abolished methylation signals when blotted with the matched antibodies.
claims.source: Interestingly, like the Gli3WT, the protein levels of Gli3K595R were still subjected to the modulation of Set7, whereas the protein levels of Gli3K436R were not responding to either knockdown or overexpression of Set7 (Figure 3C and D).
claims.evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: The methylation signals can be detected in Gli3PA but not in its arginine substitution mutants, Gli3PAK436R and Gli3PAK595R.
claims.source: Similar to the result in Figure 1H, the methylation signals can be detected in Gli3PA but not in its arginine substitution mutants, Gli3PAK436R and Gli3PAK595R when blotted with respective antibodies (Figure 1I).
claims.evidence: Shown by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1I.

claims.claim: The methylation signals on Gli3 full length were only detected in embryonic lung tissues.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4, the methylation signals on Gli3 full length were only detected in embryonic lung tissues.
claims.evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: GST-tagged Set7 can successfully pull down the flag-tagged Gli3 full-length of NIH-3T3 cells in the presence of Shh.
claims.source: GST pull-down assays indicated that GST-tagged Set7 can successfully pull down the flag-tagged Gli3 full-length of NIH-3T3 cells in the presence of Shh (Figure 1J).
claims.evidence: Shown by GST pull-down assay in Figure 1J.

claims.claim: Set7 can methylate the full-length, but not the repression form of Gli3, at K436 and K595 residues.
claims.source: Therefore, we demonstrate that Set7 can methylate the full-length, but not the repression form of Gli3, at K436 and K595 residues, indicating that Gli3 is a novel substrate of Set7.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple experiments shown in Figure 1.

claims.claim: In the absence of Shh, downregulation of Set7 had no effect on the luciferase activity.
claims.source: In the absence of Shh, downregulation of Set7 had no effect on the luciferase activity.
claims.evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Set7 knockdown dramatically decreased the luciferase activity in the presence of Shh.
claims.source: In contrast, Set7 knockdown dramatically decreased the luciferase activity in the presence of Shh, suggesting that Set7 plays a positive role on Shh pathway activation but has no effect on the basal level of Shh signaling (Figure 2A and A').
claims.evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Set7 but not its inactive mutant Set7H297A can significantly enhance the luciferase activity in the presence of Shh.
claims.source: In line with this finding, overexpression of Set7 but not its inactive mutant Set7H297A can significantly enhance the luciferase activity in the presence of Shh (Figure 2B), suggesting that its methyltransferase activity is required for Set7 mediated Shh activation.
claims.evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Set7 mediated increase of luciferase activity was in a dose-dependent manner.
claims.source: Furthermore, Set7 mediated increase of luciferase activity was in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: NIH-3T3 cells expressing Set7 siRNAs showed significant reduction in Set7 protein levels and a parallel decrease in Gli1 and Ptch1 mRNA levels compared to cells expressing control siRNAs.
claims.source: In the presence of Shh, NIH-3T3 cells expressing Set7 siRNAs showed significant reduction in Set7 protein levels and a parallel decrease in Gli1 and Ptch1 mRNA levels compared to cells expressing control siRNAs (Figure 2D–F).
claims.evidence: Shown by qPCR and western blot in Figure 2D-F.

claims.claim: Gli1 protein level was also decreased in cells with Set7 knockdown.
claims.source: In addition, Gli1 protein level was also decrease in cells with Set7 knockdown (Figure 2F).
claims.evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Either Shh or SAG, the agonist of Shh pathway, directed activation of Shh signaling can upregulate Set7 levels.
claims.source: It's of interest that either Shh or SAG, the agonist of Shh pathway, directed activation of Shh signaling can upregulate Set7 levels, whereas Gli1 knockdown can lead to a decrease of Set7 mRNA levels, suggesting the existence of a potential positive feedback loop between Set7 and Shh signaling (Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Shown by qPCR in Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Gli1 knockdown can lead to a decrease of Set7 mRNA levels.
claims.source: It's of interest that either Shh or SAG, the agonist of Shh pathway, directed activation of Shh signaling can upregulate Set7 levels, whereas Gli1 knockdown can lead to a decrease of Set7 mRNA levels, suggesting the existence of a potential positive feedback loop between Set7 and Shh signaling (Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Shown by qPCR in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: NIH-3T3 cells treated with Shh showed greatly increased methylation signals on Gli3.
claims.source: In addition, NIH-3T3 cells treated with Shh showed greatly increased methylation signals on Gli3 which may be probably due to increased Gli3 full-length or/and Set7 levels (Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the methylation signals of Gli3 is regulated by Shh input.
claims.evidence: Shown by western blot analysis in Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Set7 can positively regulate the activation of Shh signaling.
claims.source: Taken together, these findings indicate that Set7 can positively regulate the activation of Shh signaling.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple luciferase reporter assays and qPCR experiments.

claims.claim: Set7 knockdown can suppress the activation of Shh signaling, but this inhibition was abolished when the Gli3 level was depleted by RNAi.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 2G, although Set7 knockdown can suppress the activation of Shh signaling, this inhibition was abolished when the Gli3 level was depleted by RNAi.
claims.evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2G.

claims.claim: Depletion of both Gli1 and Gli2 in MEF cells showed no effect on releasing the inhibition due to Set7 knockdown.
claims.source: In contrast, depletion of both Gli1 and Gli2 in MEF cells showed no effect on releasing such inhibition due to Set7 knockdown (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: Shown by qPCR in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: The mRNA levels of Gli1 and Ptch1 and the Shh luciferase activity were decreased in cells expressing Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R compared to Gli3WT.
claims.source: Furthermore, compared to Gli3WT, the mRNA levels of Gli1 and Ptch1 and the Shh luciferase activity were decreased in cells expressing Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R, suggesting that Set7-directed Gli3 methylation plays an important role in maintaining Shh activation (Figure 2H–J).
claims.evidence: Shown by qPCR and luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2H-J.

claims.claim: Cells expressing the Gli3PA point mutants, Gli3PAK436R and Gli3PAK595R, showed decreased Shh luciferase activity and levels of Gli1 and Ptch1 transcripts compared to those with Gli3PAWT expression.
claims.source: In consistent with this finding, cells expressing the Gli3PA point mutants, Gli3PAK436R and Gli3PAK595R, showed decreased Shh luciferase activity and levels of Gli1 and Ptch1 transcripts compared to those with Gli3PAWT expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: Shown by qPCR and luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: Either Set7 downregulation or upregulation can lead to the reduction or the induction of Shh luciferase activity respectively in cells with Gli3WT expression but not in cells expressing Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R.
claims.source: Either Set7 downregulation or upregulation can lead to the reduction or the induction of Shh luciferase activity respectively in cells with Gli3WT expression but not in cells expressing Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R (Figure 2K and L).
claims.evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2K and L.

claims.claim: Gli3 methylation at K436 and K595 sites are required for Set7-mediated enhancement of Shh signaling activation.
claims.source: Thus, our findings strongly suggested that Gli3 methylation at K436 and K595 sites are required for Set7-mediated enhancement of Shh signaling activation.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple luciferase reporter assays.

claims.claim: The Gli3 accumulation on the tips of cilia was comparable among cells with Set7 knockdown, Set7 overexpression, or Set7H297A overexpression.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D, the Gli3 accumulation on the tips of cilia was comparable among those three groups, suggesting that the Set7-related changes of Shh activation are not due to the cilial translocation of Gli3.
claims.evidence: Shown by immunofluorescence staining in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Set7 caused a significant reduction of endogenous Gli3 at protein levels.
claims.source: Western blot showed that knockdown of Set7 caused a significant reduction of endogenous Gli3 at protein levels (Figure 3A, left panel), whereas overexpression of Set7 improved the Gli3 protein level (Figure 3A, right panel).
claims.evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Set7 improved the Gli3 protein level.
claims.source: Western blot showed that knockdown of Set7 caused a significant reduction of endogenous Gli3 at protein levels (Figure 3A, left panel), whereas overexpression of Set7 improved the Gli3 protein level (Figure 3A, right panel).
claims.evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: The mRNA level of Gli3 had no change regardless whether Set7 was knocked down or overexpressed.
claims.source: This Set7 mediated induction of Gli3 seems due to PTMs, because the mRNA level of Gli3 had no change regardless whether Set7 was knocked down or overexpressed (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: Shown by qPCR in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: The protein levels of Gli3K595R were still subjected to the modulation of Set7, whereas the protein levels of Gli3K436R were not responding to either knockdown or overexpression of Set7.
claims.source: Interestingly, like the Gli3WT, the protein levels of Gli3K595R were still subjected to the modulation of Set7, whereas the protein levels of Gli3K436R were not responding to either knockdown or overexpression of Set7 (Figure 3C and D).
claims.evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 3C and D.

claims.claim: The methylation at K436 but not K595 causes stability change of Gli3.
claims.source: These findings suggested that the methylation at K436 but not K595 causes stability change of Gli3 (Figure 3C and D).
claims.evidence: Inferred from western blot data in Figure 3C and D.

claims.claim: The reduced half-life of Gli3K436R, but not Gli3WT or Gli3K595R was defined by western blot in cells treated with cycloheximide (CHX).
claims.source: Finally, the reduced half-life of Gli3K436R, but not Gli3WT or Gli3K595R was defined by western blot in cells treated with cycloheximide (CHX) (Figure 3E and F).
claims.evidence: Shown by western blot and quantification in Figure 3E and F.

claims.claim: Set7 mediated methylation on K436 increases the protein stability of Gli3.
claims.source: Therefore, these data indicated that Set7 mediated methylation on K436 increases the protein stability of Gli3.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from cycloheximide chase experiments.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Set7 greatly decreased the binding of Gli3 on Gli1's promoter regions.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2, knockdown of Set7 greatly decreased the binding of Gli3 on Gli1's promoter regions (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Shown by ChIP-qPCR in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Set7 knockdown markedly affected the binding of Gli3 on Gli1's promoter regions.
claims.source: ChIP assays with anti-flag antibody demonstrated that Set7 knockdown markedly affected the binding of Gli3 on Gli1's promoter regions (Figure 3G–I), suggesting that Set7 augments the DNA binding of Gli3 full-length.
claims.evidence: Shown by ChIP-qPCR in Figure 3G-I.

claims.claim: Gli3K595R-flag showed dramatically impaired DNA binding ability, whereas the Gli3K436R-flag presented the similar DNA binding ability to Gli3WT-flag.
claims.source: ChIP assays with anti-flag antibody showed dramatically impaired the DNA binding ability in Gli3K595R-flag, whereas the Gli3K436R-flag presented the similar DNA binding ability to Gli3WT-flag (Figure 3K), suggesting that Set7 mediated methylation at K595 enhances the DNA binding ability of Gli3.
claims.evidence: Shown by ChIP-qPCR in Figure 3K.

claims.claim: Set7 mediated methylation at K595 enhances the DNA binding ability of Gli3.
claims.source: ChIP assays with anti-flag antibody showed dramatically impaired the DNA binding ability in Gli3K595R-flag, whereas the Gli3K436R-flag presented the similar DNA binding ability to Gli3WT-flag (Figure 3K), suggesting that Set7 mediated methylation at K595 enhances the DNA binding ability of Gli3.
claims.evidence: Inferred from ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 3K.

claims.claim: The binding of Gli3 to Ptch1 and Hhip promoter regions was markedly impaired after Set7 knockdown.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3, the binding of Gli3 to these regions was markedly impaired after Set7 knockdown.
claims.evidence: Shown by ChIP-qPCR in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Set7 improved the protein stability and DNA binding ability of Gli3 through methylation of K436 and K595 sites respectively.
claims.source: In conclusion, Set7 improved the protein stability and DNA binding ability of Gli3 through methylation of K436 and K595 sites respectively.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple experiments on protein stability and DNA binding.

claims.claim: Both Set7 and Gli1 were extensively expressed in A549 cells.
claims.source: By comparison on the mRNA levels of Set7 and Gli1 between Beas2B, a normal bronchial epithelial lung cell line, and A549, a non-small cell lung cancer cell line, we found that both Set7 and Gli1 were extensively expressed in A549 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Shown by qPCR in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The GEO database search (GSE10245) showed a positive association between Set7 and Gli1 in NSCLC tumor samples.
claims.source: Furthermore, the GEO database search (GSE10245) showed a positive association between Set7 and Gli1 in NSCLC tumor samples, suggesting the involvement of this Set7-Gli3-Gli1 axis in the development of NSCLCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Shown by correlation analysis in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Depletion of Set7 displayed a decreased luciferase activity and reduced expression of Gli1 and Ptch1 in A549 cells.
claims.source: Depletion of Set7 displayed a decreased luciferase activity and reduced expression of Gli1 and Ptch1 (Figure 4A and B).
claims.evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay and qPCR in Figure 4A and B.

claims.claim: Compared to A549 cells with stable Gli3WT expression, reduced luciferase activity and transcripts of Gli1 and Ptch1 were detected in cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR.
claims.source: Compared to A549 cells with stable Gli3WT expression, reduced luciferase activity and transcripts of Gli1 and Ptch1 were detected in cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR (Figure 4C–E).
claims.evidence: Shown by western blot, qPCR, and luciferase reporter assay in Figure 4C-E.

claims.claim: More severe suppression on luciferase activities and Ptch1 mRNA, but not Gli1 mRNA, was observed in cells expressing Gli3KRKR.
claims.source: In addition, more severe suppression on luciferase activities and Ptch1 mRNA, but not Gli1 mRNA, was observed in cells expressing Gli3KRKR, suggesting that the methylation at these two sites plays a synergistic role in regulating Shh signaling activation (Figure 4D and E).
claims.evidence: Shown by qPCR and luciferase reporter assay in Figure 4D and E.

claims.claim: MTT assays showed attenuated growth in cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR compared to cells with Gli3WT expression.
claims.source: In line with the reduced Shh activation, MTT assays showed attenuated growth in cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR compared to cells with Gli3WT expression (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: Shown by MTT assay in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: The ability to form colonies in soft agar was dramatically impaired in stable transfectants with the expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR compared to Gli3WT.
claims.source: The ability to form colonies in soft agar was dramatically impaired in stable transfectants with the expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR compared to Gli3WT (Figure 4G and G').
claims.evidence: Shown by soft agar assay in Figure 4G and G'.

claims.claim: A549 cells with stable expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR showed retarded tumor growth in a xenograft tumor model.
claims.source: In agreement with these in vitro growth assays, A549 cells with stable expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR showed retarded tumor growth in a xenograft tumor model (Figure 4H–J).
claims.evidence: Shown by xenograft tumor experiments in Figure 4H-J.

claims.claim: A549 cells with the expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR had limited migration ability compared to Gli3WT.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4K and L, A549 cells with the expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR had limited migration ability compared to Gli3WT.
claims.evidence: Shown by wound healing and transwell migration assays in Figure 4K and L.

claims.claim: The invasion ability of A549 cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR was substantially reduced.
claims.source: Furthermore, matrigel chamber assays were performed and the invasion ability of A549 cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR was substantially reduced (Figure 4M).
claims.evidence: Shown by matrigel invasion assay in Figure 4M.

claims.claim: All the in vitro functional experiments in Figure 4 were repeated in A549 cells stably transfected with Gli3PAWT, Gli3PAK436R, Gli3PAK595R or Gli3PAKRKR, and showed similar results.
claims.source: Moreover, all the in vitro functional experiments in Figure 4 were repeated in A549 cells stably transfected with Gli3PAWT, Gli3PAK436R, Gli3PAK595R or Gli3PAKRKR, and showed similar results (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Shown by multiple assays in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The methylation on Gli3 full-length regulates tumorigenesis in NSCLCs.
claims.source: It further confirms that the methylation on Gli3 full-length regulates tumorigenesis in NSCLCs.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments with Gli3PA mutants.

claims.claim: Set7 can exclusively methylate Gli3 full-length at K436 and K595 sites in vitro and in vivo.
claims.source: In present study, we demonstrated that Set7 can exclusively methylate Gli3 full-length at K436 and K595 sites in vitro and in vivo.
claims.evidence: Summary of experimental findings from in vitro and in vivo methylation assays.

claims.claim: These methylations on Gli3 augment the activation of Shh signaling.
claims.source: These methylations on Gli3 augment the activation of Shh signaling.
claims.evidence: Summary of luciferase reporter assays and qPCR experiments.

claims.claim: Gli3 is a novel substrate of Set7.
claims.source: To our knowledge, we for the first time identified Gli3 as a novel substrate of Set7 and demonstrated the involvement of Set7 in Shh activation.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple experiments showing Set7-mediated Gli3 methylation.

claims.claim: Set7 is involved in Shh activation.
claims.source: To our knowledge, we for the first time identified Gli3 as a novel substrate of Set7 and demonstrated the involvement of Set7 in Shh activation.

results.result: Set7 specifically methylates Gli3 full-length at K436 and K595 residues in vitro and in vivo, but not the truncated Gli3 repressor form. Mass spectrometry identified these methylation sites, which are evolutionarily conserved and show sequence similarity to known Set7 substrates. In vitro methylation assays, immunoprecipitation experiments, and GST pull-down assays confirmed Set7-mediated methylation at these sites, with arginine substitution mutants (K436R, K595R) abolishing methylation signals.
results.evaluation: The result is well-supported by multiple complementary experimental approaches including mass spectrometry (C19, C21), in vitro methylation assays (C23, C24), immunoprecipitation with site-specific antibodies (C26-C32), and GST pull-down assays (C25, C34). The use of arginine substitution mutants as negative controls strengthens the specificity claims. The evolutionary conservation (C22) and sequence similarity to known Set7 substrates (C20) provide additional supporting evidence.

results.result: Set7 positively regulates Shh signaling activation through Gli3 methylation. Set7 knockdown decreases luciferase activity and expression of Shh target genes (Gli1, Ptch1) in the presence of Shh, while Set7 overexpression enhances signaling in a dose-dependent manner requiring its methyltransferase activity. The effect requires Gli3 but not Gli1/Gli2, and unmethylatable Gli3 mutants (K436R, K595R) show reduced Shh signaling activation. A positive feedback loop exists where Shh/SAG upregulates Set7 levels.
results.evaluation: The result is strongly supported by multiple luciferase reporter assays (C36-C39, C48, C50), qPCR measurements of target genes (C40, C48), and genetic epistasis experiments (C46, C47) demonstrating Gli3-dependence. The requirement for Set7's methyltransferase activity is shown by the inactive mutant control (C38). The dose-dependent effect (C39) and rescue experiments with unmethylatable mutants (C48-C50) provide strong mechanistic evidence. The positive feedback loop (C42, C43) is supported by qPCR data.

results.result: Set7-mediated methylation at K436 increases Gli3 protein stability. Set7 knockdown reduces Gli3 protein levels while overexpression increases them, without affecting Gli3 mRNA levels. The Gli3K436R mutant shows reduced protein stability and half-life compared to wild-type Gli3 or Gli3K595R, as demonstrated by cycloheximide chase experiments. The Gli3K436R mutant protein levels do not respond to Set7 modulation, while Gli3K595R levels remain responsive.
results.evaluation: The result is well-supported by western blot analysis showing protein level changes (C53, C54), qPCR showing no mRNA changes (C55), differential responses of mutants to Set7 modulation (C56), and cycloheximide chase experiments demonstrating reduced half-life of Gli3K436R (C58). The specificity for K436 versus K595 in stability regulation (C57) is clearly demonstrated through mutant analysis. The combination of gain-of-function, loss-of-function, and protein half-life measurements provides strong evidence.

results.result: Set7-mediated methylation at K595 enhances Gli3 DNA binding ability. ChIP assays show that Set7 knockdown markedly reduces Gli3 binding to promoter regions of target genes (Gli1, Ptch1, Hhip). The Gli3K595R mutant shows dramatically impaired DNA binding compared to wild-type Gli3, while Gli3K436R maintains similar DNA binding ability. K595 is located in the zinc finger domain important for DNA binding.
results.evaluation: The result is strongly supported by ChIP-qPCR experiments at multiple target gene promoters (C60, C61, C64) and comparison of mutants showing specific impairment of K595R but not K436R in DNA binding (C62). The structural context provided by K595's location in the zinc finger domain (C98) supports the mechanistic interpretation. Multiple independent ChIP experiments with different antibodies strengthen the conclusion.

results.result: Set7-mediated effects on Shh signaling are not due to altered Gli3 ciliary translocation. Gli3 accumulation at cilia tips was comparable among cells with Set7 knockdown, Set7 overexpression, or catalytically inactive Set7H297A overexpression, despite these conditions showing different Shh signaling activities.
results.evaluation: The result is supported by immunofluorescence quantification showing no significant differences in Gli3 ciliary localization across different Set7 conditions (C52). This negative result is important for ruling out an alternative mechanism and is appropriately controlled with both knockdown and overexpression conditions, as well as the catalytically inactive mutant. The statistical analysis showing no significant differences strengthens this conclusion.

results.result: Gli3 methylation by Set7 contributes to tumor growth and metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Set7 and Gli1 are highly expressed in A549 NSCLC cells and show positive correlation in NSCLC tumor samples. A549 cells expressing unmethylatable Gli3 mutants (K436R, K595R, or double mutant KRKR) show reduced Shh signaling, decreased cell proliferation (MTT, soft agar assays), retarded tumor growth in xenograft models, and impaired migration and invasion abilities compared to wild-type Gli3.
results.evaluation: The result is comprehensively supported by multiple in vitro functional assays (C71, C72, C74, C75), in vivo xenograft experiments (C73), correlation analysis in patient samples (C67), and validation with Gli3PA mutants (C76). The use of single and double mutants (C69, C70) demonstrates both individual and synergistic effects of the two methylation sites. The consistency across multiple assay types (proliferation, colony formation, migration, invasion, tumor growth) strengthens the conclusion about the oncogenic role.

results.result: Gli3 methylation signals were detected specifically in embryonic lung tissues among multiple mouse embryonic tissues examined (brain, lung, skin, skeleton, gut) at 14.5 days post coitum.
results.evaluation: While the western blot data shows methylation signals in lung tissue (C33), the result is limited by the lack of quantification, unclear sample sizes, and no discussion of why methylation is tissue-specific or what this means functionally. The biological significance of this tissue-specific pattern is not explored, and it's unclear whether this represents true tissue specificity or differences in Gli3 expression levels or Shh pathway activity across tissues.

results.result: The authors propose that Lsd1 demethylase may remove Gli3 methylation in the nucleus, and that increased Set7 levels in response to Shh signaling could compensate for Lsd1-mediated demethylation. They also speculate that Set7 may be a key regulator of WNT-Shh pathway crosstalk.
results.evaluation: These claims are purely speculative (C87, C88, C91) without any experimental evidence. No experiments with Lsd1 knockdown, overexpression, or inhibition are presented. No direct evidence of WNT-Shh crosstalk regulation by Set7 is provided. While the speculation is reasonable based on prior literature about Lsd1 and Set7's role in WNT signaling (C90, C96), these remain untested hypotheses that require experimental validation.

results.result: The two methylation sites (K436 and K595) on Gli3 are functionally non-redundant, as arginine substitution at either site severely impairs Shh signaling activation, suggesting Set7 fine-tunes Gli3 transactivity through both modifications.
results.evaluation: This conclusion is well-supported by the data showing that single mutations at either K436 or K595 each significantly reduce Shh signaling (C48, C62), and that the double mutant shows even greater effects on some readouts (C70). The distinct mechanisms (stability vs. DNA binding) by which each site functions (C3, C4, C57, C63) support the non-redundancy claim.

results.result: The authors suggest that Set7 has therapeutic value in targeting Shh-dependent tumors such as basal cell carcinoma (BCC), medulloblastoma (MB), and lung cancer.
results.evaluation: While the NSCLC data (C5, C73, C83) supports a role in lung cancer, the claim about therapeutic value in BCC and MB is purely speculative without any experimental evidence in these cancer types. The therapeutic potential claim requires additional validation including specificity studies, off-target effects analysis, and demonstration that Set7 inhibition would be effective and safe. The leap from mechanistic studies to therapeutic value is not sufficiently supported.
